Count history of one species: detections per site and occasion

Source: R/07_count_history.R
pam_count_history.Rd

Counts the detections of one species in each site and occasion of a project and returns them in the form that abundance models need: a matrix with sites in rows and occasions in columns, NA where a site was not surveyed, and matrices of recording effort and days. This is the abundance counterpart of the detection histories of Stage 6.

Usage

pam_count_history(
  cfg,
  species,
  run_id = cfg$birdnet$run_id,
  bin_days = NULL,
  count = c("events", "files"),
  thresholds = NULL,
  min_effort_hours = NULL,
  site_covariates = NULL
)

Arguments

cfg

A pam_config object.

species

The species, given as scientific name, common name or species label (any capitalisation). It must identify exactly one species.

run_id

Detection run (sub-folder of paths$detections).

bin_days

Length of an occasion in days. NULL uses occupancy$occasion_length_days (1 if not set).

count

What to count: "events" (the default; detected events, which Stage 4 forms by merging overlapping BirdNET windows) or "files" (the number of recordings with at least one detection, which cannot exceed the number of recordings and is less affected by one animal calling for a long time).

thresholds

Optional per-species thresholds (a data frame, or the path of a CSV file, with scientific_name and threshold), for example from pam_species_thresholds().

min_effort_hours

Minimum recorded hours for an occasion to count as surveyed; others are NA. NULL uses occupancy$min_effort_hours (2 if not set).

site_covariates

Optional data frame of site covariates with a site_id column (for example habitat or elevation). Every site must have a row.

Value

An object of class pam_count_history: a list with

  • y: integer matrix of counts (sites x occasions, NA = not surveyed);

  • effort: matrix of recorded hours (NA where not surveyed);

  • day: matrix of days since the first occasion;

  • site_covariates: data frame with site_id and your covariates;

  • occasions: the start and end day of each occasion;

  • species, count: what was counted.

Details

Sites and occasions follow Stage 6: occasions are blocks of bin_days days starting on the first recorded day, shared by all sites, and only occasions with recordings at some site appear. The counts are numbers of detections, not numbers of animals, so models fitted to them give a relative abundance index. Use pam_model_input() to turn the history into input for abundance or occupancy models.

See also

pam_as_count_history(), pam_model_input()

Examples

ex <- pam_example_project()
#> Error in pam_example_project(): could not find function "pam_example_project"
# the later stages read the master table that the scan builds
res <- suppressMessages(pam_scan_audio(ex$cfg))
#> Error: object 'ex' not found
proc <- suppressMessages(pam_process_detections(ex$cfg))
#> Error: object 'ex' not found
sp <- unique(proc$clean$scientific_name)[1]
#> Error: object 'proc' not found
hist <- suppressMessages(pam_count_history(ex$cfg, species = sp))
#> Error in pam_count_history(ex$cfg, species = sp): could not find function "pam_count_history"
hist$y
#> Error in hist$y: object of type 'closure' is not subsettable
